formReason: Soft and hard delete answer the same decision: an accidental delete favours soft, while an erasure request and a re-used unique email favour hard.
title: When should a delete really delete?
hook: One keeps a promise, one breaks it
origin: The card says soft delete is safer without asking safer for what

points.body: A flag marks the row as gone. It is still stored, still indexed, and still counts against constraints.
The row is gone from the live table. Recovery now depends on backups, which is a far slower path.
With soft delete, each read must remember the filter. One forgotten query shows deleted data.

anchor.note: The bin lets you change your mind; only the shredder lets you say the paper no longer exists.

card.a: Soft delete keeps a recovery path. Hard delete is required when data must truly be removed.

situations.label: A user deleted the wrong order

soft.text: Clear the flag and it is back

hard.text: Gone unless a backup holds it

situations.why: Soft delete never gave up the data, so undo costs one update.

situations.label: A legal erasure request arrives

soft.text: The personal data is still stored

hard.text: The live data is really gone

situations.why: Erasure is about what you hold, and a hidden row is still held.

situations.label: The same email signs up again

soft.text: Unique index hits the hidden row

hard.text: The email is free to use

situations.why: A unique constraint sees every row unless the index excludes deleted ones.

contrast.verdict: Need undo: soft. Must erase: hard.
